data.body_html:
July in Marbella is the golden month for boating: the Mediterranean is warm, the sun is relentless, and the coastline glitters from Puerto Banús to Estepona. With average highs of 31°C and sea temperatures of 24°C, conditions are near-perfect for a day on the water. But peak season means planning ahead—here's your essential guide to renting a boat in Marbella in July, with honest advice on weather, timing, and the best boats for the heat.

July Weather in Marbella: What to Expect

July delivers the Costa del Sol's most reliable boating weather. Expect clear skies, 11+ hours of sunshine, and a UV index of 9—pack SPF 50. Sea swells typically range from 0.3 to 0.5 metres, with winds of 10–15 knots, often picking up slightly in the afternoon. Air temperatures peak around 31°C, cooling to a pleasant 23°C in the evening.

Visibility is excellent, often exceeding 20 nautical miles, so you'll see the Sierra Blanca and La Concha from the water. The Levante wind can occasionally bring a chop, but our skippers know the sheltered coves, like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, where you'll stay comfortable.

Why July is Peak Season for Boat Rentals

July is the busiest month on the Marbella coast. Schools are out, resorts are full, and the demand for charters spikes. That means two things: incredible energy on the water and limited availability. Boats like the Astondoa 40 and Azimut 39 are often booked days ahead, especially for weekend slots. The Mangusta 80, with its 4-hour minimum, is a favourite for group celebrations.

To secure your preferred vessel, book at least 2–3 weeks in advance. For last-minute requests, contact us via WhatsApp—we'll do our best to match you with an available boat from our fleet.

Best Times to Sail: Beat the Heat

July sun is intense, so timing matters. Early morning charters (09:00–13:00) offer calm seas and cooler air—ideal for a leisurely cruise to Cabopino or a swim stop at Cala Cortés. Late afternoon (17:00–20:00) brings a refreshing sea breeze and golden light, perfect for sunset photos with the Marbella skyline behind you.

Midday heat can be fierce, but boats with flybridges or covered cockpits—like the Azimut 58 Flybridge or Ferretti 94—provide shade. Alternatively, opt for a fast open boat like the Pershing 46 to create your own breeze.

Choosing the Right Boat for July Conditions

For small groups (up to 9), the Astondoa 40 (12.5m) or Azimut 39 (12.5m) are excellent value at €749 for 2 hours or €2,299 for 8 hours. Both depart from Puerto Banús and include a skipper, drinks, and snacks. For larger parties, the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax) is a showstopper—€4,719 for 4 hours, with a jet ski included free.

If you're after speed and agility, the Fairline Targa 12m (10 pax) or Pershing 46 (10 pax) are great picks. For a relaxed catamaran vibe, the Lagoon 380 (10 pax) offers stability and space. All our boats are maintained to high standards and come with a licensed skipper.

What's Included in Your July Charter

No hidden costs—every charter includes:

  • Licensed skipper and fuel
  • Water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava
  • Light snacks
  • Insurance and safety equipment
  • Spanish IVA (21%)

For Mangusta 80 charters, a jet ski is included free. Just bring your sunscreen and swimwear. Our skippers are local experts and can tailor the route to your preferences, whether that's anchoring off the Golden Mile or exploring the cliffs near Estepona.

July Boating Destinations from Puerto Banús

From Puerto Banús, you have a wealth of options. Head east to Cabopino for quiet coves and clear water, or west to Estepona for a charming marina lunch. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are top spots for swimming and snorkelling, with July water clarity at its best.

For a longer excursion, Sotogrande is a 45-minute cruise where you can spot dolphins. If you prefer to stay close, anchor off Río Verde and watch the yachts drift by. Our skippers know the best anchorages based on wind and swell.

Booking Tips for July

Book early, be flexible with timing, and communicate your group size. For the best value, consider a weekday charter—demand is lower than weekends. If you're set on a specific boat like the Mangusta 80, confirm availability via WhatsApp before finalising plans.

Remember that July is hot—bring a hat, sunglasses, and plenty of sunscreen. Most boats have shaded areas, but the sun is strong. And don't forget your camera for those unforgettable sunset shots over La Concha.
